close_reason: Added 3 integration tests in crate-jmap-metadata-server/tests/metadata_tests.rs covering negative-position clamp-from-end, over-large-negative clamp-to-zero, and positive-position clamp-to-len behavior. All three pass on first run; the existing implementation matches RFC 8620 §5.5. The i64-to-u64 cast structural concern raised by the bead is in scope of the workspace-canonical-first epic JMAP-pgj7 (lossy as-casts in query pagination).
description:
Trigger: client supplies position: -5 in /query against MemoryBackend. memory.rs:594-599 handles negative position by ids.len().saturating_sub(neg). For a small object set (e.g. 3 objects, position=-100), start becomes 0 (correct). But the position field reported back in QueryResult is 'start as u64' (memory.rs:609) — which loses the i64 signedness. RFC 8620 §5.5 says position is the 0-based index from start of results.

Less severe than the filter-no-op finding above, but worth filing because:
(a) the i64-to-u64 cast in memory.rs:609 happens through saturating logic that silently coerces — a future caller who passes a negative position and expects an echo back of the same negative number gets a clamped 0/N value with no diagnostic.
(b) RFC 8620 §5.5 says position can be negative in the request (offset from end) but the response always echoes a non-negative position. The current impl computes position correctly but the test surface against MemoryBackend has no coverage for this path.

This is reference-impl-quality, not production. But the rustdoc on memory.rs:5-13 calls itself a 'reference implementation' to study. The negative-position contract is one of the easier-to-get-wrong corners of /query.

Probe (do not run): integration test asserts that handle_metadata_query with position=-1 and 3 objects returns position=2 (or similar correct value) and a single-item ids array. Currently would need to be verified to be sure the i64-to-u64 cast does the right thing across edge cases.
notes: Re-classifying as P2 efficiency/edge-case: the negative-position path computes correctly (saturating_sub handles overflow), and an unfiltered total is consistent with the unfiltered behavior. The concern is reference-impl documentation/quality, not a correctness bug.
title: MemoryBackend.query_objects total reports unfiltered count; QueryResult.position is u64 but i64 input negative offsets are accepted (silent semantic drift)
